_comment: Machine-readable transcription of updates/2026-11-23-peer-claim-verification.md (Group A defects raised against me, Group B peer landed-claims). expected_verdict is the verdict the hand-written report recorded, so tools/verify_peer_claims.py can self-check against it. Do NOT edit expected_verdict to make the script agree - report a disagreement instead.
_origin_reachable_definition: A commit is origin-reachable when it is an ancestor of origin/main OR sits on some refs/remotes/origin/* ref. A commit that exists only locally is NOT LANDED by definition.
_polarity_definition: Every check carries an explicit polarity. 'supports': PASS is evidence FOR the claim, FAIL is evidence AGAINST. 'refutes': PASS is evidence AGAINST the claim, FAIL is evidence FOR. Absence checks (path_absent_from_main, commit_absent, commit_not_reachable) are 'refutes' - finding X missing is evidence against a claim that X landed. The engine tallies supporting vs refuting: no executable check -> UNVERIFIABLE; 0 refuting and >=1 supporting -> VERIFIED; >=1 refuting and 0 supporting -> NOT LANDED; both -> PARTIALLY.
_ref_definition: Every check accepts an optional 'ref' (default: the CLI --ref, origin/main). A ref that is not resolvable in this clone is looked up in the repos given by --remote-map / VERIFY_EXTRA_REMOTES ({remote name: local git path}); e.g. 'review/main' works when --remote-map '{"review": "/path/to/review-clone"}' is given. An unresolvable ref makes the check SKIP, never FAIL.
